draft.tex in the workspace is a short paper draft. Review it with one script program that you write yourself (the script tool's description lists what a program can call):
1. Get the draft's sections through the latex script module.
2. Run two review rounds with self(), each returning a structured verdict that names the section it checked and whether its claim is supported. Round 1 checks the first section; choose round 2's section from round 1's verdict.

Return an object with the section titles, both verdicts, and that count as completedChildren. Then reply with one sentence on what the review found.

The claim it makes: it stipulates K compact and f continuous (defining hypotheses), no mathematical assertion. So supported: false — it asserts nothing derivable / makes no claim that can be supported. Provide reasoning.

input.claim: The section claims only that $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is compact and $f\colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous; it asserts no substantive mathematical result of its own.
input.reasoning: The section is purely stipulative: it introduces a compact set $K$ and a continuous real-valued function $f$ on it, and stops there. Nothing is proved, bounded, or derived, so there is no substantive claim for the draft to support — a hypothesis-only setup makes no derivable claim. Note also that no compactness consequence (e.g. $f$ attains a finite maximum) is stated, so even that much is left implicit. Consequently the section cannot carry the later assertion $\sup_K|f| \le 1$; that claim belongs to "Main bound", which merely announces it while explicitly omitting the proof, so it will need to be examined next.

Section title: "Main bound". Claim: sup_K |f| ≤ 1. supported: false.

Reasoning: The section asserts a uniform bound with no hypothesis tying f to 1 (only compactness/continuity from Setup, which allows arbitrarily large constants), and explicitly omits the proof. No derivation, no assumptions, so unsupported.

followUpSection: "Discussion".

input.claim: For every compact K ⊂ ℝⁿ and continuous f : K → ℝ, sup_K |f| ≤ 1.
input.reasoning: The section only asserts the bound and states "The proof is omitted," so nothing in the draft derives it. The only available hypotheses (Setup: K compact, f continuous) do not constrain the size of f at all — e.g. f ≡ 2 on any nonempty compact K satisfies both hypotheses with sup_K |f| = 2 > 1, so the claim is not merely unproved but false as stated. No normalization, boundedness, or integral constraint is assumed anywhere. Hence the claim is unsupported.
